headline: AI agents can be tricked via public forms, exposing CRM data
summary: SalesBleed vulnerability demonstrated how prompt injection in public forms can lead to sensitive data exfiltration from CRMs.
details: A new vulnerability, dubbed SalesBleed, has been demonstrated by Zenity Labs, showing how AI agents interacting with public forms can be manipulated to exfiltrate sensitive CRM data. The attack exploits prompt injection within standard web forms, such as 'contact us' pages, which are publicly accessible.

The attack vector involves an attacker submitting a form with hidden instructions within one of the fields. When an AI agent later processes this data, it can be tricked into executing these hidden commands, potentially accessing and transmitting data beyond its intended scope.

Salesforce has since patched the specific flaws reported by Zenity Labs on June 1st. While no real-world exploitation was reported, the underlying vulnerability pattern remains relevant wherever AI agents process free-text input from untrusted sources.

Developers are advised to consider the implications of AI agents reading external text. Instead of solely focusing on blocking injections, it's crucial to limit what an agent can do *after* being compromised. This includes restricting direct tool access, validating input formats, and implementing strict output controls.

The article suggests a multi-layered approach: a local AI model with limited capabilities, a JSON grid for structured output with predefined verdicts (GO, NO_GO, UNKNOWN), and strict format checks. Crucially, the system rereads raw text for key criteria to override any manipulated model responses.

Further checks include validating extracted information against unambiguous keywords from the original text and limiting the size of input fields to mitigate potential overflow attacks or excessive data processing.

OWASP ranks prompt injection as the number one risk for LLM-based applications. While no filter is foolproof, implementing robust post-compromise controls significantly reduces the potential damage from such attacks.
